Kenett Ponce-Zamora in Auckland, New Zealand

Kenett spent the spring semester in Auckland, New Zealand at the University of Auckland . Interested in going far for your semester abroad? Kenett can tell you what to expect from life and travel in New Zealand.
I had so much fun! I even joined the club UoA Buddies, where I was connected with a buddy leader and other students that were on exchange, so we could see and learn about Auckland together.

Get to know life in a small Dutch town in Maastricht, Netherlands to study abroad at Maastricht University Center for European Studies! Maastricht is located at the southern most region of the Netherlands, nestled between Germany and Belgium. Classes are taught in English with smaller cohorts of students, focusing of problem-based learning to encourage flexibility in education. Students are required to take a class either in the Dutch language or culture while in attendance and are housed with other international students. Studying close to three separate countries and with a plethora of people from different countries allows for easy access to experience a wide variety of cultures without having to go far. The first two weeks of the program will be an introductory workshop and Dutch Discovery Trip, exploring the surrounding area and Maastricht city tour. Students are also offered a weekend trip to Paris, France and day trip to the Belgian Caves of Han and Val-Dieu Abbey. Maastricht University Center for European Studies is perfect for students who want the chance to explore not just Dutch culture, but the many that surround it, too.

Jelila Adedoyin Surakat in Cape Town, South Africa
The emergence of Amapiano dance and music, and my interest in its connection to Hip-Hop, House, and West African styles of dance, inspired my selection of South Africa as my study abroad destination.

My host parents made me f eel like I truly had a home in Chile. It’s one thing to travel to places and stay in hotels/Airbnbs, but living in a Chilean couple’s apartment with them made it feel like I was a part of their family. I truly felt safe and cared for in their apartment and knew that I had a loving home to return to each day and after each trips, and a happy couple who would be excited to welcome me back.
Angelina Lopez in São Paulo, Brazil
I loved my all my roommates. I got super close with all of them and Amanda, our Brazilian roommate, loved to show us around the city, and teach us new words.

Studying abroad was an incredible experience, and all the people I met there truly made it amazing. It is not only possible to go abroad, but you also have the tools necessary for a successful experience from USC.

While studying abroad, I was able to take courses for my Philosophy, Politics, and Law major and my Spanish minor. I also learned how to talk about law in Spanish and identify differences between the American and Argentinian legal systems.

I chose IES Abroad in Berlin because I thought that living in the capital would allow me to experience the full range of experiences that Germany has to offer. After completing my program, I am happy to say that it met and actually exceeded my expectations!

Sometimes being away from the comfort of home leads to some loneliness, but I found that the more I surrounded myself with good people and friends, this homesickness slowly subsided. Being in a foreign country is definitely a shock in the beginning, but before you know it, you’ll start to feel comfortable.

Everyone in the program stayed in the same complex. I got lucky and was placed in a single, but there were also some doubles. By living in the same place as all my friends I was able to spend so much time with them exploring the city and relaxing. My friends and I started playing DnD, and I had frequent walks, study days, or movie nights with my friend Jaid who lived a floor up from me. The housing situation really helped create a community for us.
